title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting
excerpt:
4. Model Description

This section describes the dropout neural network model. Consider a neural network with L hidden layers. Let l ∈ {1, ..., L} index the hidden layers of the network. Let z^(l) denote the vector of inputs into layer l, y^(l) denote the vector of outputs from layer l (y^(0) = x is the input). W^(l) and b^(l) are the weights and biases at layer l. The feed-forward operation of a standard neural network can be described as (for l ∈ {0, ..., L−1} and any hidden unit i)

z_i^(l+1) = w_i^(l+1) y^(l) + b_i^(l+1),
y_i^(l+1) = f(z_i^(l+1)),

where f is any activation function, for example, f(x) = 1/(1 + exp(−x)).

With dropout, the feed-forward operation becomes

r_j^(l) ∼ Bernoulli(p),
ỹ^(l) = r^(l) ∗ y^(l),
z_i^(l+1) = w_i^(l+1) ỹ^(l) + b_i^(l+1),
y_i^(l+1) = f(z_i^(l+1)).

Here ∗ denotes an element-wise product. For any layer l, r^(l) is a vector of independent Bernoulli random variables each of which has probability p of being 1. This vector is sampled and multiplied element-wise with the outputs of that layer, y^(l), to create the thinned outputs ỹ^(l). The thinned outputs are then used as input to the next layer. This process is applied at each layer. This amounts to sampling a sub-network from a larger network.

At test time, the weights are scaled as W_test^(l) = p W^(l) as shown in Figure 2. The resulting neural network is used without dropout.
focus: The dropout feed-forward operation and test-time weight scaling (Section 4): a Bernoulli(p) mask thins a layer's outputs during training; at test time weights are multiplied by p. Use one small layer with a few units feeding one linear unit. Let the learner change the retention probability p and resample the mask with a seed. Compare the training-time pre-activation for one mask, its exact expectation over masks, and the test-time value with scaled weights. Check: the expected training-time pre-activation equals the test-time pre-activation.
audience: Engineering undergraduates who know what a weighted sum and an expected value are.
